properties.rationale:
Anthony's word, 2026-08-24, after being walked through the six open gaps: the work is DONE and the gap is the detector applying a code-shaped rule to a model-only change.

VERIFIED BEFORE ACKNOWLEDGING, not taken on the status field: the committed export was read directly, and all five kernel components — cmp:nodes, cmp:schema, cmp:identity, cmp:graph, cmp:provenance — are now contained by ONE subsystem. The bisection that produced the sys:store ↔ sys:vocabulary cycle is gone.

WHY NO ARTIFACT WILL EVER REALIZE THIS. The capability's own text says it: "PURE MODEL BOOKKEEPING — not one line of Rust changes." Its `delivery` is `model`. The deliverable WAS the decomposition, and the decomposition is what changed. `unrealized_capability` asks "what actually gets built for it?" and the honest answer is "nothing is built; the model is the product." Pointing some Rust file at it to close the gap would be worse than leaving it open — it would assert that a file implements a containment decision.

⭐ THE GENERAL FORM, worth more than this one acknowledgement: a capability whose delivery is `model` cannot satisfy an artifact-shaped check. If this recurs often enough to be noise, the detector should read `delivery` rather than every model change needing a hand-written acknowledgement.

ALSO SETTLED IN PASSING: the capability's text carried an open sub-question — whether sys:store still deserved that name once it meant "the foundation everything is built on". The subsystem is now named `sys:foundation`, so the naming call was made in the direction the note anticipated.
